entries.name: INSTANCE_NAME
entries.description: Display name of the business this instance serves.
howToGet: Use the business's public name.

entries.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
entries.description: Permanent id of the business. Every row in the database is tagged with it.
howToGet: Lowercase the business name and replace spaces with dashes. Never change it after the first deploy.

entries.name: ENABLED_INTEGRATIONS
entries.description: Comma-separated catalog ids of the integrations this instance uses. Secrets for an integration are only required once it is listed here, and each built connector listed syncs on a schedule.
howToGet: Start empty and add each integration as you connect it.

entries.name: SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES
entries.description: Minutes between the end of one sync round and the start of the next, for every connector listed in ENABLED_INTEGRATIONS.
howToGet: Leave empty for 60. Use 5 to 1440.

entries.name: FEEDBACK_COOLDOWN_DAYS
entries.description: Days a dismissed recommendation's rule and subject is held back before it is raised again, unless its dollar estimate or confidence grew. 0 turns the cooldown off.
howToGet: Leave empty for 14. Use 0 to 90.

entries.name: REASON_SCHEDULE
entries.description: Scheduled reasoning: the department rules run after each sync round that brings new events, before the daily brief and at least every REASON_INTERVAL_MINUTES. off leaves reasoning to POST /v1/reason.
howToGet: Leave empty for on.
Use off only when something else calls POST /v1/reason on a schedule.

entries.name: REASON_INTERVAL_MINUTES
entries.description: The longest gap, in minutes, between the end of one scheduled reasoning run and the start of the next, when no sync round has brought new events.
howToGet: Leave empty for 60. Use 5 to 1440.

entries.name: INSTANCE_API_KEY
entries.description: Key that agents and connectors send to call this instance's API.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.

entries.name: SUPPORT_API_KEY
entries.description: Optional key for support access: it reaches only GET /healthz, GET /v1/integrations and GET /v1/support/status (names, timings and counts), never the client's business data. Must differ from INSTANCE_API_KEY. Leave it unset to turn support access off.
howToGet: Generated by npm run secrets:setup -- --purposes core,instance,migrations,support when the client agrees to support access.
Give it only to whoever supports the instance. Remove it from the host's secret store to turn support access off.

entries.name: WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET
entries.description: Signs and verifies webhooks this instance sends or receives.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup.

entries.name: SUPABASE_URL
entries.description: Address of this client's own Supabase project.
howToGet: Open supabase.com/dashboard and pick this client's project (each client gets its own).
Go to Project Settings > API.
Copy the Project URL.

entries.name: SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
entries.description: Public (anon or publishable) key for the same Supabase project.
howToGet: In the same Supabase project, go to Project Settings > API.
Copy the anon public key (or the publishable key).
It must come from the same project as SUPABASE_URL, or Supabase answers HTTP 401.

entries.name: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
entries.description: Server-only key that bypasses row-level security. Never put it in a browser or app.
howToGet: In the same Supabase project, go to Project Settings > API and copy the service_role (or secret) key.

entries.name: SUPABASE_DB_URL
entries.description: Direct Postgres connection string. The instance uses it to store data and run migrations.
howToGet: In the same Supabase project, click Connect at the top of the dashboard.
Copy the URI connection string (Session pooler works everywhere).
Replace [YOUR-PASSWORD] with the database password you set when creating the project.

entries.name: DOC_REGISTRY_IDS
entries.description: Comma-separated ids of the source-of-truth docs reasoning must consult. Optional, but without it every recommendation is marked degraded.
howToGet: Leave as is unless you maintain your own documentation registry.

entries.name: ENABLED_WRITES
entries.description: Comma-separated writes to outside systems this instance allows. Empty keeps every integration read-only.
howToGet: Leave empty. Every integration starts read-only.
Only after the client agrees in writing, list the exact actions, e.g. shopify:adjust_inventory, or shopify:* for every Shopify action.

entries.name: ENABLED_DEPARTMENTS
entries.description: Comma-separated retail departments this instance runs. Empty runs all of them.
howToGet: Leave empty to run every retail department.
To start smaller, list only the ids from docs/departments/README.md that the store uses.

entries.name: RAW_RETENTION_DAYS
entries.description: Days raw vendor data is kept before it is cleared. Facts, signals and links back to the source stay.
howToGet: Leave empty to keep 30 days.
Set a whole number from 1 to 365 if the client's policy asks for a different window.

entries.name: STORE_TIME_ZONE
entries.description: The store's IANA time zone. The daily brief's days start and end at the store's midnight, and it is built at BRIEF_HOUR on the store's clock.
howToGet: Leave empty for America/New_York.
Otherwise use the store's zone from the IANA list, such as America/Chicago or America/Los_Angeles.

entries.name: BRIEF_HOUR
entries.description: The hour on the store's clock, 0 to 23, from which yesterday's daily brief is built.
howToGet: Leave empty for 7, so the brief is ready at 7 in the morning.

entries.name: STORE_HOURS
entries.description: When the store is open, on STORE_TIME_ZONE's clock: days or day ranges, then 24-hour times on the quarter hour or closed, entries separated by semicolons. Clienteling's awaiting-reply rule counts only these hours. A day left out is closed, and a range past midnight is rejected.
howToGet: Leave empty for mon-sat 10:00-18:00; sun closed.
Otherwise copy the hours the store posts, e.g. tue-sat 10:00-13:00, 14:00-19:00 for a store that closes for lunch. See docs/deployment/instances.md#store-hours.

entries.name: STORE_CLOSED_DATES
entries.description: Days the store is shut whatever STORE_HOURS says, such as holidays, as comma-separated YYYY-MM-DD dates on the store's calendar.
howToGet: Leave empty when the store keeps to its weekly hours.
List the year's holidays the store closes for; dates that have passed can stay.

entries.name: AWAITING_REPLY_HOURS
entries.description: Open hours, 1 to 72, a customer's message waits with no answer on any channel before clienteling raises it.
howToGet: Leave empty for 4.

entries.name: BENCH_STAGE_LIMIT_DAYS
entries.description: Whole days, 1 to 365, a bench job can sit in a stage before it is raised as stuck: one number for every stage, stages of their own such as casting=5, setting=3, or both.
howToGet: Leave empty for design 7, casting 4, setting 4, finishing 3, qc 2 and on_hold 14 days.
Set the stages the workshop's own pace differs on.

entries.name: BENCH_METAL_LOSS_PERCENT
entries.description: The metal a bench job may lose across its stages, as a percent of the most issued to it, above 0 and up to 50, before the bench department raises it.
howToGet: Leave empty for 3.
Set it to the loss the workshop accepts on a job, casting included.

entries.name: BENCH_LABOR_RATE
entries.description: What an hour of bench time costs the shop, in dollars from 1 to 1000: one figure for everyone, jewelers' own such as Ana=55, or both. Production planning prices each piece's bench minutes with it.
howToGet: Leave empty for $45 an hour.
Set it to wages and what comes with them, per bench hour; give a jeweler their own where it differs.

entries.name: BENCH_DAILY_HOURS
entries.description: Hours of bench work a jeweler does in a working day, 0.5 to 24: one figure for everyone, jewelers' own such as Ben=4, or both. Production planning compares the work queued with them over the next 7 days.
howToGet: Leave empty for 6 hours.
Count the hours at the bench, not the hours in the building.

entries.name: BRIEF_WEBHOOK_URL
entries.description: Optional https address the daily brief is posted to as JSON each morning, such as a chat tool's incoming webhook. Treated as a secret because such addresses usually carry a token. Leave it unset and the brief is only saved and served by GET /v1/brief.
howToGet: Create an incoming webhook in the tool the owner wants the brief in and copy its https address.
Put it only in the host's secret store. Remove it to stop sending the brief.
